MATHEMATICAL ANALYSIS AND CALCULUS FORMULAS

FUNDAMENTAL OPERATORS AND DERIVATIVES
The Derivative of a real single-variable function represents the instantaneous rate of change of the output with respect to the input:
f'(x) = \lim_{h \to 0} \frac{f(x + h) - f(x)}{h}

Common Differentiation Rules:
Function | First Derivative
c | 0
x^n | n * x^{n-1}
sin(x) | cos(x)
cos(x) | -sin(x)
e^x | e^x
ln(x) | 1/x

The Chain Rule states that the derivative of a composite function f(g(x)) is the product of outer and inner derivatives:
\frac{d}{dx}[f(g(x))] = f'(g(x)) * g'(x)

INTEGRAL CALCULUS AND ACCUMULATION
The Indefinite Integral represents the continuous family of antiderivative functions:
\int f(x) dx = F(x) + C, where F'(x) = f(x)

The Fundamental Theorem of Calculus connects differentiation and definite integration:
\int_a^b f(x) dx = F(b) - F(a)

Integration by Parts is derived from the product rule of differential calculus:
\int u dv = u v - \int v du
